text:
amelia: heads up — CI flaked on PR 21321. microbench `kv_warmup_unit_test` shows p95 tail latency +28% vs main on the autoselect change. cc @raj @sasha :eyes:

raj: saw it. repro on my laptop with the same seed. interestingly the p50 is stable, p95 and p99 blow up during the first 200ms of the run (warmup). suspect kernel selection + batch timer interaction. logs: `kernel_autoselect: using kernel v2 -> v3` then kv hits drop.

sasha: sharing the CI job link and raw artifacts: https://ci.redwood/archived/21321/kvsample.zip :link: contains perf-prof, flamegraphs, and kernel selector trace.

mateo: tagging infra-bot to pull the node-level metrics during the failed job. @infra-bot can you attach gpu/host perf samples?

infra-bot: attached: host-counters.json, nvprof-sample.tar.gz, and node-metrics.csv (job 21321 run 7).

raj: quick summary from the flamegraph: CPU thread doing batch coalescing spends ~30% more time in `choose_kernel()` on this run; KV cache lookup latency increased by ~40us per lookup during warm path. That matches the kv hit-rate dip in the telemetry.

taylor: did we change any KV bucket sizing or eviction policy in this PR? I only saw kernel-autoselect heuristics touched.

amelia: the PR only touched kernel-autoselect thresholds and a small batching timer tweak: `batch_timer_ms = max(1, heuristic * 2)` (see diff: https://git.redwood/pr/21321/files). No direct kv changes.

sasha: attaching a minimal repro snippet I used locally:
```
python perf_repro.py --model tiny --seed 42 --seq-len 128 --batcher=continuous --warm=200 --trace=select.log
```
Run that twice, first with `main` kernel selector, then with PR branch to compare. I can share my traces.

raj: I ran a quick bisect across the autoselect commits in the PR. Narrowed to the commit that changed the kernel candidate ordering when seq_len < 256. Reproduces locally.

mateo: is this a rollout blocker? We have a few customers on dedicated where warmup tail matters.

amelia: yes, it's a rollout blocker for Dedicated (SLO risk). Proposal: revert the ordering change and push a hotfix while we investigate deeper. Thoughts? :thumbsup::thumbdown:

taylor: +1 revert until we understand why candidate ordering interacts with KV warmup. We should also add a perf unit that simulates KV-heavy warmups.

raj: agree. I'll prepare a small revert PR and add an extended microbench that runs multiple short sequences interleaved with KV lookups to catch regressions.

sasha: also propose adding a short flamegraph capture step in CI perf jobs when threshold diffs exceed 10% so we have artifacts attached automatically. The current artifacts were manual.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-412 to add flamegraph capture on perf CI exceed thresholds.

ci-bot: CI job 21321 run 7 status: failed (perf-threshold). Threshold diff: p95 +28%. See artifacts at https://ci.redwood/job/21321/7/artifacts

amelia: plan of action:
1) @raj open revert PR for the autoselect ordering (hotfix branch).
2) @raj add the microbench extension and a reproducible test.
3) @sasha attach repro traces and write a short investigation doc with flamegraphs.
4) infra to file capture automation (INFRA-412).
5) run canary after revert and watch Dedicated warmup graphs for 24h.

raj: will do, opening revert PR now: https://git.redwood/pr/21345 (WIP).

mateo: i'll watch the canary post-revert and alert if p95 > baseline.

sasha: filing a short postmortem draft in GH gist and will link once ready.

amelia: thanks folks. if anyone finds extra telemetry (kv bucket distribution, slab churn), paste it here. Let's try to have the revert landed in the next hour if possible. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: revert PR submitted and CI started. keeping this thread updated.

ci-bot: CI check for PR 21345: perf unit tests started. ETA ~12m.

amelia: great — keeping this thread pinned for the rollback window.
